label: Late original-phase s/v/t-type input after a sequence opening with o/h/r/0/3/j/f
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at positions 3-8, peaking at t=4-6 (97% of mass); essentially never at t<2 or in the copy phase, and weakly on <DEL> (3%). Two things combine. (1) The current input: s is by far the strongest (36% of mass, 8.8x lift), then v and t (~16% each), then weaker q, w, k, p, u, 1. (2) Which tokens opened the sequence: rates are about 3x higher when the first tokens are from {o,h,r,3,0,j,f}. The top activations are s right after an opener like h h c / h o r l / r h 0 y, often right after another active q/w/v step, and activation tends to carry onto the next one or two inputs. It also mostly fires on the first occurrence of a token (92% of mass). It does not fire on other letters or in sequences that open with other tokens. The behavior looks like an additive mix of input identity and prefix contents, so a boolean predicate only captures it in part (dev F1 about 0.42; mass recall 0.56 for this predicate, and about 0.84 with a looser opener condition at precision 0.23).
